facts.fact: It was built as the headquarters of PPG Industries (Pittsburgh Plate Glass), and all its buildings share a matching glass design of 19,750 pieces.
facts.quote: Named for its anchor tenant, PPG Industries, which initiated the project for its headquarters, the buildings are all of matching glass design consisting of 19,750 pieces of glass.

facts.fact: Designed in a neo-Gothic style with modern innovations, it drew on London's Victoria Tower, Richardson's Allegheny County Courthouse and the Cathedral of Learning.
facts.quote: Designed in the neogothic style but with modern innovations, the complex had many inspirations, including London's Victoria Tower, and H. H. Richardson's Allegheny County Courthouse and Charles Klauder's Cathedral of Learning in Pittsburgh.

facts.fact: The buildings are known for their 231 glass spires, the tallest 82 feet (25 m) high.
facts.quote: The buildings are recognized by their 231 glass spires, with the largest one 82 feet (25 m) tall.

facts.fact: The centrepiece, One PPG Place, is a 40-storey tower; the complex also has a 14-storey building and four 6-storey ones.
facts.quote: The primary building, One PPG Place, is a 40-story tower, with PPG Industries occupying half of the space. The complex also contains a 14-story building, and four 6-story structures.

facts.fact: The glass reflects summer heat away and keeps infrared heat inside in winter, and the building recycles heat from computer equipment.
facts.quote: Heat in the summer is reflected away from the building by the glass, while in winter infrared heat is reflected and contained within the building. The surface walls feature a barrier construction that effectively separates the interior walls from the exterior. The building also collects heat from computer equipment and recycles it throughout the structure.

facts.fact: Its plaza is turned into an ice-skating rink in winter.
facts.quote: During the winter months, the plaza is converted into an ice skating rink.

facts.fact: On completion, critics called it "the crown jewel in Pittsburgh's skyline".
facts.quote: Upon completion of the project, architectural critics and the media called PPG Place "the crown jewel in Pittsburgh's skyline," "the towering success of downtown Pittsburgh," and "one of the most ambitious, sensitive and public spirited urban developments since Rockefeller Center."

facts.fact: Hallfield Primary School is a Grade II* listed primary school on the Hallfield Estate in Westminster, built in 1953–1955 to Denys Lasdun's design.
facts.quote: It is a grade II* listed building in Inverness Terrace on the Hallfield Estate in Westminster, built in 1953–1955 and designed by Denys Lasdun.

facts.fact: The school was the first sign of Lasdun's mature style, with its bare concrete and angular forms at a more human scale.
facts.quote: Lasdun's Hallfield School was the first clue to his mature style, in its use of bare concrete and angularity, as well as its more human scale.

facts.fact: After the war Lasdun worked with Lindsay Drake on the Hallfield Estate, first planned by Berthold Lubetkin and Tecton.
facts.quote: After the war, Lasdun worked with Lindsay Drake on the Hallfield Estate, which had been planned by Lubetkin and Tecton in a similar patterned, tightly planned idiom to his Spa Green and Priory Green Estates.

facts.fact: By the 1970s the school was overcrowded; in 2005 two new buildings by Caruso St John were added, winning a RIBA Award in 2006.
facts.quote: The original school designed by Denys Lasdun in the 1950s had become overcrowded by the 1970s. In 2005, new funding allowed two new buildings designed by Caruso St John to be added. These were a RIBA Award Winner in 2006.

facts.fact: Sert designed the Joieria J. Roca jewellery shop at 18 Passeig de Gràcia, Barcelona, in 1933–1934; it is now a Rolex boutique.
facts.quote: 1933–1934: Joieria J. Roca (currently, Boutique Rolex) at 18, Passeig de Gràcia, Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain

facts.fact: The Jardinette Apartments, now called the Marathon Apartments, is a four-storey apartment building in Hollywood, Los Angeles, designed by Richard Neutra.
facts.quote: Jardinette Apartments, now known as Marathon Apartments, is a four-story apartment building in Hollywood, Los Angeles, California, designed by modernist Richard Neutra. It was Neutra's first commission in the United States.

facts.fact: It was Neutra's first commission in the United States, and Richard Weston called it one of the first Modernist buildings in America.
facts.quote: It was Neutra's first commission in the United States. In his book Key Buildings of the Twentieth Century, Richard Weston called the Jardinette Apartments "one of the first Modernist buildings in America."

facts.fact: Neutra built it in reinforced concrete, whose long spans allowed unbroken strips of windows; the original design also had rooftop gardens.
facts.quote: Neutra chose reinforced concrete for Jardinette, with long spans of reinforced concrete allowing for unbroken window strips. The original design also included rooftop gardens.

facts.fact: The main block runs east to west along the back of the site, with a short wing at each end forming a shallow courtyard.
facts.quote: The building's main structure runs east to west along the back of the site, with two short wings at either end forming a shallow courtyard.

facts.fact: It was meant as the prototype for a series of garden apartments in Hollywood, but the developer went bankrupt during construction and the others were never built.
facts.quote: The Jardinette was intended as a prototype for a series of garden apartments to be built in Hollywood. However, the developer, Joseph H. Miller, went bankrupt during the construction of Jardinette, and the other buildings were never realized.

facts.fact: It was one of the few American examples in the Museum of Modern Art's 1932 exhibition "Modern Architecture".
facts.quote: At the Museum of Modern Art's famed 1932 exhibition entitled "Modern Architecture," Neutra's Jardinette Apartments was one of the few American examples included in the exhibition.

facts.fact: Its lack of ornament set it apart from other Los Angeles apartment buildings of the 1920s.
facts.quote: One of the key features that set the Jardinette apart from other apartment buildings built in Los Angeles in the 1920s was the lack of ornamentation.

facts.fact: The building was listed in the National Register of Historic Places in 1986.
facts.quote: In 1986, the Jardinette was listed in the National Register of Historic Places.

facts.fact: The Märkisches Museum, founded in 1874 as the museum of Berlin and the March of Brandenburg, occupies a building by Ludwig Hoffmann facing the Spree, completed in 1908.
facts.quote: Founded in 1874 as the museum of the city of Berlin and its political region, the March of Brandenburg, it occupies a building on the northern edge of Köllnischer Park, facing the Spree, which was designed by Ludwig Hoffmann and completed in 1908.

facts.fact: It was Hoffmann's first large task after he became Berlin's chief of construction in 1896; building began in 1899 and finished in 1907.
facts.quote: Creating a new building for the museum was the first large task for Ludwig Hoffmann after his appointment in 1896 as Stadtbaurat (chief of construction) for the city of Berlin. His first sketches date to that year; the plans were accepted the following year, and construction began in 1899 and was completed in 1907.

facts.fact: Hoffmann designed it as a group of six different buildings echoing Brandenburg brick architecture from Gothic to Renaissance, a "historical collage" reflecting the collection.
facts.quote: Hoffmann designed the museum as a complex of six differing buildings which echo Brandenburg brick architecture of periods from the Gothic to the Renaissance in a "historical collage", in order to reflect the contents of the museum and evoke the "atmosphere" of various times and types of building.

facts.fact: The buildings are grouped around two courtyards and copy historic details Hoffmann had sketched across the region; the 53-metre tower is said to follow the keep of the Bishop's Castle in Wittstock or Ratzeburg Cathedral.
facts.quote: The buildings are grouped around two courtyards and based on historic details which he had studied and sketched throughout the region; his "quotations" are accurate copies, but there is disagreement as to the originals, as in a façade which has been said to be based on the town hall at Tangermünde or on St. Catherine's Church in Brandenburg an der Havel, and the hip-roofed tower, 53 metres (174 ft) high, based on the bergfried (keep) of the Bishop's Castle in Wittstock or on the cathedral of Ratzeburg.

facts.fact: Inside, each gallery was made to evoke a period: low vaults and rough plaster for prehistory, a vaulted Gothic chapel for medieval altars.
facts.quote: For example, the low vaulted ceilings and roughly plastered walls on the ground floor were intended to suggest great age and housed the displays on prehistory, where the display cases for funerary urns and flint axes were rough in form; the setting for the medieval altars and sculptures was a vaulted Gothic chapel echoing medieval church interiors; weapons were shown in a room with thick columns, recalling a monastery; and rococo porcelain and snuffboxes were displayed in elegant vitrines in a light and airy room on the second floor.

facts.fact: There were about 50 galleries, and visitors were led back again and again to the central vaulted Great Hall.
facts.quote: There were a total of about 50 exhibition galleries. The visitor was led repeatedly back to the central vaulted Great Hall.

facts.fact: The museum is now judged among Hoffmann's most important works and one of the most outstanding German museum buildings.
facts.quote: The museum is now judged to be amongst Hoffmann's most important works, and also one of the most outstanding German museum buildings.

facts.fact: The museum closed for extensive renovation in 2023 and is planned to reopen by 2029.
facts.quote: The museum closed for extensive renovations in 2023. Reopening is planned by 2029.

facts.fact: The Kollhoff Tower is a 25-storey, 103-metre skyscraper on Potsdamer Platz in Berlin, completed in 1999 after four years of construction.
facts.quote: Kollhoff-Tower is a 25-story, 103 metres (338 ft) skyscraper on the Potsdamer Platz in Berlin, Germany. The building, named after Hans Kollhoff from Kollhoff und Timmermann Architekten, was completed in 1999 after four years of construction.

facts.fact: With the Bahntower to the north and Renzo Piano's Forum Tower to the south, it forms a high-rise ensemble in the middle of the city.
facts.quote: Together with the Bahntower 103 metres (338 ft) to the north and the Forum Tower designed by Renzo Piano (together with Atrium Tower and The Playce shopping center part of the debis complex) to the south, it forms a high-rise ensemble in the middle of the city.

facts.fact: Like Kollhoff's nearby Delbrück high-rise, it is designed in the style of early 20th-century high-rise architecture.
facts.quote: Kollhoff and Timmermann Architekten also designed the nearby Delbrück high-rise of the Beisheim Center. Both buildings are designed in the style of early 20th century high-rise architecture.

facts.fact: Kollhoff designed it for DaimlerChrysler in an old-New York brick style.
facts.quote: In Berlin, he has designed in Potsdamer Platz a high-rise tower in an old-New York brick style, for DaimlerChrysler.

facts.fact: The lowest floors hold shops and the upper floors offices.
facts.quote: The lowest floors are intended for retail outlets, while the upper floors are reserved for offices.

facts.fact: Since 2000 a viewing platform has been open at the top, reached by the fastest passenger lift in Europe, at 8.65 m per second.
facts.quote: Since April 15, 2000, there has been a viewing platform on the top level, to which the fastest passenger elevator in Europe leads. It transports passengers at 8.65 m per second.

facts.fact: Moisture getting into the clinker brick facade can cause frost damage, so the facade was scaffolded for repairs in 2009.
facts.quote: At the beginning of 2009, the building was scaffolded for façade repairs. Moisture penetrating the clinker façade can cause frost damage, which can lead to parts of the façade falling off.

facts.fact: The James A. Farley Building, New York's former main post office, was designed by McKim, Mead & White in the Beaux-Arts style and built 1911–1914, with an annex of 1932–1935.
facts.quote: Designed by McKim, Mead & White in the Beaux-Arts style, the structure was built between 1911 and 1914, with an annex constructed between 1932 and 1935.

facts.fact: It is a four-storey steel-frame building clad in granite, fronted on Eighth Avenue by a colonnade of twenty 53-foot Corinthian columns.
facts.quote: The four-story structure consists of granite ashlar cladding around a steel-frame superstructure. The monumental facade on Eighth Avenue was conceived as a Corinthian colonnade, composed of twenty 53-foot-tall (16 m) columns.

facts.fact: The colonnade was meant to match the colonnade of the same firm's original Pennsylvania Station across the avenue.
facts.quote: The imposing design was meant to match the strength of the colonnade of McKim, Mead, and White's original Pennsylvania Station across Eighth Avenue, which originally faced the General Post Office Building.

facts.fact: The entablature carries the inscription "Neither snow nor rain nor heat nor gloom of night…", taken from Herodotus.
facts.quote: An entablature above the colonnade bears the inscription "Neither snow nor rain nor heat nor gloom of night stays these couriers from the swift completion of their appointed rounds". The sentence is taken from Herodotus' Histories (Book 8, Ch. 98) and describes the faithful service of the Persian system of mounted postal messengers under Xerxes I of Persia.

facts.fact: The building became a New York City landmark in 1966 and was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1973.
facts.quote: The building was made a New York City designated landmark in 1966 and was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1973.

facts.fact: Since 2021 the former main mail sorting room has housed Moynihan Train Hall.
facts.quote: The interior space that once housed the main mail sorting room now houses the Moynihan Train Hall since 2021.

facts.fact: Skidmore, Owings & Merrill designed the hall: a passenger concourse under a 92-foot-tall glass skylight, with a four-faced clock at its centre.
facts.quote: The 486,000 sq ft (45,200 m2) complex was designed by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM). It consists of a 31,000 ft2 (2,900 m2) passenger concourse underneath a 92 ft (28 m) tall glass skylight.

facts.fact: The $1.6 billion project restored parts of the Farley Building and added a glass-roofed central atrium, shops and a waiting area.
facts.quote: The $1.6 billion renovation produced a 486,000 ft2 (45,200 m2) complex. Besides restoring portions of the Farley Building, the project added a central atrium with a glass roof, retail space, a 320-seat waiting area for ticket-holding passengers, and public restrooms.

facts.fact: The Kulturpalast Dresden is a modernist building by Wolfgang Hänsch from the GDR era; when it opened in 1969 it was Dresden's largest multi-purpose hall.
facts.quote: The Kulturpalast Dresden (lit. 'Palace of Culture') is a modernist building designed by Wolfgang Hänsch during the era of the German Democratic Republic. It was the largest multi-purpose hall in Dresden when it opened in 1969, and was used for concerts, dances, conferences and other events.

facts.fact: Unlike the other buildings on the Altmarkt it is in the unadorned International Style, and is seen as a sister building to Berlin's demolished Palast der Republik.
facts.quote: Unlike the other buildings in the Altmarkt square, the Kulturpalast is designed in the unadorned International Style; it is considered a sister building to the now-demolished Palast der Republik in Berlin.

facts.fact: It was first planned as a Socialist Classicist high-rise in the style of Moscow's Seven Sisters.
facts.quote: The Kulturpalast was planned as a Socialist Classicist ensemble building. The intention was to erect a high-rise building in the style of the Seven Sisters in Moscow.

facts.fact: A "tilting parquet" let the original hall work either as a 2,435-seat auditorium with raked seating or as a flat banquet floor.
facts.quote: Due to a special "tilting parquet", the Kulturpalast's original multi-functional ballroom could be used as either a 2435-seat auditorium with rising rows of seats or as a level banquet area.

facts.fact: The west side carries a 30-by-10.5-metre mural, "The Way of the Red Flag", made of concrete slabs coated with coloured glass.
facts.quote: There is a 30-by-10.5-metre (98 ft × 34 ft) mural on the west side of the building, designed by Gerhard Bondzin and created in 1969 by a working group from the Dresden Academy of Fine Arts. The mural, titled Der Weg der roten Fahne (The Way of the Red Flag), is made of concrete slabs electrostatically coated with colored glass.

facts.fact: The building closed in 2012 and reopened in April 2017 with a new concert hall designed by Gerkan, Marg and Partners.
facts.quote: The building closed for extensive renovations in July 2012. Exterior construction work began in October 2013. The new concert hall, designed by Gerkan, Marg and Partners, reopened in April 2017.

facts.fact: Today it also houses the main branch of the Dresden City Libraries and a cabaret stage.
facts.quote: As well as the main hall, the building now houses the main branch of the Dresden City Libraries and a performance space used by the cabaret group Die Herkuleskeule.

facts.fact: Utrecht's main city theatre was built by Dudok in 1941.
facts.quote: The 1941 main city theatre was built by Dudok.

facts.fact: The National Space Centre in Leicester is a museum and educational centre for space science and astronomy, with a research programme run with the University of Leicester.
facts.quote: The National Space Centre is a museum and educational resource covering the fields of space science and astronomy, along with a space research programme in partnership with the University of Leicester.

facts.fact: Upright rockets stand in a tower with minimal steel supports and semi-transparent cladding of ETFE pillows, now one of Leicester's best-known landmarks.
facts.quote: Many of the exhibits, including upright rockets are housed in a tower with minimal steel supports and a semi-transparent cladding of ETFE 'pillows', which has become one of Leicester's most recognisable landmarks.

facts.fact: Nicholas Grimshaw's practice, architects of the Eden Project, won the design competition in September 1996.
facts.quote: Nicholas Grimshaw, the architects of the Eden Project, won an architectural competition to design the National Space Centre in September 1996 beating four other architects.

facts.fact: The scheme sits on a former storm-water tank, reused as the building's foundations to cut costs.
facts.quote: The 7,360m2 scheme occupies a former storm water tank, which now forms the foundations of the building, reducing costs and maximising the reuse of the existing structure.

facts.fact: The rocket tower's ETFE pillows, the same material as the Eden Project domes, weigh 1% of the equivalent glass.
facts.quote: The main rocket tower is clad in inflated pillows made of ETFE – the same material used on the Eden Project domes. This material is 1% of the weight of the equivalent amount of glass.

facts.fact: The main building is a box on a 14 m steel grid, wrapped in perforated metal, and its gravel roof forms a Crab Nebula pattern in three colours.
facts.quote: The main building is a 7200m2 box built on a 14m grid steel frame, clad in a perforated metal skin that conceals the windows and louvres in the profiled steel cladding behind. The roof of the main building is overlaid with gravel in three colours to form a crab nebulae design.

facts.fact: The tower is 42 metres tall.
facts.quote: The tower is 42 m (138 ft) tall and claims to be the only place to house upright space rockets indoors, although from Nov 2026 the California Science Center will open an indoor exhibit containing the Space Shuttle Endeavour upright in launch configuration with external fuel tank and solid rocket boosters.

facts.fact: It opened to the public on 30 June 2001.
facts.quote: On 30 June 2001, former NASA astronaut Jeffrey A. Hoffman opened the National Space Centre officially to the general public.

facts.fact: Place Bonaventure is an office, exhibition and hotel complex in downtown Montreal, next to Central Station; at completion in 1967 it was the world's second-largest commercial building.
facts.quote: Place Bonaventure (French pronunciation: [plas bɔnavɑ̃tyʁ]) is an office, exhibition, and hotel complex in Downtown Montreal, Quebec, Canada, adjacent to the city's Central Station. At 288,000 m2 (3,100,000 sq ft)  in size, Place Bonaventure was the second-largest commercial building in the world at the time of its completion in 1967.

facts.fact: It covers two hectares built over 18 railway tracks leading to Central Station, and was built 1964–1967.
facts.quote: The building covers an area of 2 ha (4.9 acres) and is built over 18 CNR tracks leading to Central Station. Construction began in 1964 and was completed in 1967.

facts.fact: It is Brutalist: the outer walls are poured-in-place, ribbed, sand-blasted concrete.
facts.quote: Designed in the Brutalist style, the exterior walls are poured-in-place, ribbed sand-blasted concrete, with the interior walls sand-blasted concrete or brick.

facts.fact: It is one of the major projects of the Montreal firm Arcop, along with Place Ville-Marie and Maison Alcan.
facts.quote: Arcop (also ARCOP) was an architectural firm based in Montreal, renowned for designing many major projects in Canada including Place Bonaventure, Place Ville-Marie and Maison Alcan.

facts.fact: It held Concordia Hall, a 23,000 m² exhibition hall, which hosted its first trade show in 1966 while the upper floors were still being built.
facts.quote: Concordia Hall was a 23,000 m2 (250,000 sq ft) exhibition hall. The first trade show was hosted in 1966, while the upper floors were still being constructed.

facts.fact: A 397-room hotel sits on the roof, with a heated outdoor pool and a 2.5-acre rooftop garden.
facts.quote: The complex houses a 397-room rooftop hotel, Hotel Bonaventure Montreal (formerly a Westin then a Hilton Hotel), featuring a year-round heated rooftop outdoor pool, a 2.5-acre rooftop garden with trees, flowers and waterfalls, a jacuzzi, and a dry sauna.

facts.fact: A CAD$60 million renovation in 1998 redesigned it as large, continuous office space.
facts.quote: In 1998 Place Bonaventure was renovated at an expense of CAD$60 million. The building was redesigned to offer large, continuous office space.

facts.fact: It is connected to Montreal's underground city.
facts.quote: Place Bonaventure is connected to Montreal's underground city.

facts.fact: The Lowry stands at the end of Pier 8 at Salford Quays, almost surrounded by the Manchester Ship Canal.
facts.quote: The Lowry stands at the end of Pier 8, largely surrounded by the waters of the Manchester Ship Canal.

facts.fact: Designed by James Stirling and Michael Wilford, it opened on 28 April 2000 with a 1,730-seat theatre, a 466-seat theatre, studios and galleries.
facts.quote: Designed by James Stirling and Michael Wilford, it opened on 28 April 2000 and houses the 1,730 seat Lyric theatre, the 466 seat Quays theatre, studio spaces and 17,330 sq ft (1,610 m2) of gallery space.

facts.fact: The centre is linked to the painter L. S. Lowry and holds a collection of his work.
facts.quote: The centre is associated with L. S. Lowry, and houses a collection of his work.

facts.fact: A landmark arts venue was planned from 1988 as part of the Salford Quays regeneration and became the Lowry Project in 1994.
facts.quote: Early in the planning stages for redevelopment of Salford Quays in 1988, potential was recognised for a landmark arts venue, the Salford Quays Centre for the Performing Arts, which became known as the Lowry Project in 1994. It had secured £64 million in funding by 22 February 1996.

facts.fact: It won the Royal Fine Art Commission Building of the Year Award in 2001.
facts.quote: These projects have won many architectural awards, the most recent including The Royal Fine Art Commission Building of the Year Award in 2001 for The Lowry performing and visual arts centre in Salford, England.

facts.fact: The school's most famous building was designed by Charles Rennie Mackintosh and Margaret Macdonald Mackintosh in phases between 1896 and 1909.
facts.quote: The most famous of its buildings was designed by Charles Rennie Mackintosh and Margaret Macdonald Mackintosh in phases between 1896 and 1909. The eponymous Mackintosh Building soon became one of the city's iconic landmarks, of international fame.

facts.fact: It is a pioneer of the Modern Style, the British form of Art Nouveau.
facts.quote: It is a pioneer of the Modern Style (British Art Nouveau style).

facts.fact: The school's director Francis Newbery chose Mackintosh; the first half was finished in 1899 and the second in 1909.
facts.quote: The building was designed by Charles Rennie Mackintosh, chosen for the commission by the school's director, Francis Newbery, who oversaw a period of expansion and fast-growing reputation. The first half of the building was completed in 1899 and the second half in 1909.

facts.fact: It was the project that made Mackintosh's international reputation.
facts.quote: The project that helped make his international reputation was the Glasgow School of Art (1897–1909).

facts.fact: Critics cite the Mackintosh Building as among the finest buildings in the UK.
facts.quote: The Glasgow School of Art building (now "The Mackintosh Building") is cited by architectural critics as among the finest buildings in the UK.

facts.fact: A fire in May 2014 destroyed the famous library, and the restoration used original woods such as longleaf pine and tulipwood.
facts.quote: A careful restoration process began soon after the fire; work on restoring and recreating the Mackintosh design, including the famous library interior, started in 2016. The restoration was performed with historical accuracy, including the use of original wood species such as longleaf pine and tulipwood.

facts.fact: A second fire in June 2018 left only a burnt-out shell; there are plans to rebuild it in Mackintosh's style.
facts.quote: The building was severely damaged by fire in May 2014 and destroyed by a second fire in June 2018, with only the burnt-out shell remaining. Plans are in place for its rebuilding in accordance with Charles Rennie Mackintosh's style and content.

facts.fact: The Pampulha Art Museum is one of Belo Horizonte's museums.
facts.quote: Belo Horizonte features a number of museums including the Mineiro Museum, the Abílio Barreto Historic Museum, Arts and Workmanship Museum, a Natural History Museum and the UFMG Botanic Gardens, a telephone museum, the Pampulha Art Museum, the Professor Taylor Gramke Mineralogy Museum, and the UFMG Conservatory.

facts.fact: In the 1940s a young Oscar Niemeyer designed the Pampulha neighbourhood to great acclaim, a commission he owed to the mayor Juscelino Kubitschek.
facts.quote: In the 1940s a young Oscar Niemeyer designed the Pampulha Neighbourhood to great acclaim, a commission he got thanks to then-mayor and soon-to-be-president Juscelino Kubitschek.

facts.fact: The ICA's current home in Boston's South Boston Seaport District was built in 2006 to a design by Diller Scofidio + Renfro.
facts.quote: Its current home was built in 2006 in the South Boston Seaport District and designed by architects Diller Scofidio + Renfro.

facts.fact: It was among the firm's first buildings, its first in the United States, and the first new art museum in Boston in over a century.
facts.quote: It is one of that firm's first structures to be built, and the first to be built in the United States. It is also the first new art museum to be built in Boston in over a century.

facts.fact: The ICA won a competition in 1999 to build a new cultural building on Boston's Fan Pier.
facts.quote: Then, in 1999 the ICA won a competition to build a new cultural institution building on Boston's Fan Pier.

facts.fact: The 65,000-square-foot building holds both galleries and a performance space.
facts.quote: In 2006 the ICA moved to its new 65,000 square foot building on Fan Pier containing both galleries and a performance space.

facts.fact: Its design echoes the nearby waterfront gantry cranes, and critics praised its openness, its outdoor grand staircase and the way it embraces the harbour.
facts.quote: The building's design, which echoes that of nearby waterfront gantry cranes, has been celebrated by many critics for its openness, represented by its exterior grand staircase, and willingness to embrace the surrounding harbor.

facts.fact: It won the 2007 Harleston Parker Medal for the most beautiful piece of architecture in Boston.
facts.quote: The ICA was the recipient of the 2007 Harleston Parker Medal, awarded to "the most beautiful piece of architecture" in Boston.

facts.fact: The critic Philip Nobel called it a "botched box", faulting its circulation, its dull land-side facade and the shadow it casts on the harbourside promenade.
facts.quote: It has also been called a "botched box" by architecture critic Philip Nobel, who criticised it for having poor circulation, a dull façade facing land, and casting into shadow the harborside promenade that Elizabeth Diller once referred to as "Boston's only viable civic space."

facts.fact: The Everson Museum of Art in downtown Syracuse focuses on American art.
facts.quote: The Everson Museum of Art ( EE-vər-sən) in Downtown Syracuse, New York, is a major Central New York museum focusing on American art.

facts.fact: Helen Everson's $1 million gift of 1941 paid for the building; ground was broken in 1965 and the new museum opened in 1968.
facts.quote: In 1941, Helen Everson made a $1 million gift to the city of Syracuse to fund the construction of an art museum. A groundbreaking took place in 1965, and in 1968 the new Everson Museum of Art opened.

facts.fact: The new building was designed by I. M. Pei and is seen as a work of art in its own right.
facts.quote: The new building was designed by architect I. M. Pei and is regarded as a work of art in its own right.

facts.fact: Pei conceived it as a sculptural object set against the city's modern architecture, not simply a "monumental container for art".
facts.quote: I.M. Pei conceived it as a sculptural object set against the city's modern architecture, not simply a "monumental container for art." The four cantilevered square volumes reinforce this quality.

facts.fact: Four cantilevered square volumes give it that sculptural quality, and its blank facades are often used as screens for films and images.
facts.quote: The four cantilevered square volumes reinforce this quality. The exterior facades often serve as projection surfaces for films and images, with community members gathering in the neighboring courtyard to watch.

facts.fact: Its plaza became a famous skateboarding spot from the mid-1980s, called by some an "East Coast skate mecca".
facts.quote: Skateboarders started skating at the Everson Museum of Art in the mid-1980s. The museum is a famous location for skateboarders, considered by some an "East Coast skate mecca."

facts.fact: Hans Scharoun built the Geschwister-Scholl-Schule in Lünen in 1956–62 as a girls' school; it is now a comprehensive school.
facts.quote: Girls School (now a comprehensive school) "Geschwister-Scholl-Schule", Lünen, (1956–62)

facts.fact: It is one of the post-war buildings in which Scharoun realised his ambitious and humanistic idea of architecture, alongside the Berlin Philharmonie.
facts.quote: After the war he was able to realise his architectural understanding, both ambitious and humanistic, in exemplary buildings; e.g., in the Stuttgart apartment towers of Romeo und Julia (Hochhäuser) (1954–59), in the Geschwister-Scholl-Gesamtschule Lünen (1956–62) and in the famed concert hall Berliner Philharmonie (1956–63).

facts.fact: The school shares a differentiated organisation of space with these buildings and is planned like a small city.
facts.quote: Common to all these buildings is a differentiated organization of space. The school is planned like a small city, and the apartment towers allow for allocation of space and function.

facts.fact: Palazzo Piccolomini stands in the centre of Pienza next to the cathedral; built from 1459 to Bernardo Rossellino's design, it is one of the earliest examples of Renaissance architecture.
facts.quote: Palazzo Piccolomini ("Piccolomini Palace" in English) is a palace in the center of Pienza, Italy, next to the Duomo. Palazzo Piccolimini is one of the earliest examples of Renaissance architecture and was built starting in 1459 to a design by Bernardo Rossellino.

facts.fact: Pope Pius II, born in the village later renamed Pienza after him, commissioned it.
facts.quote: It was commissioned by Pope Pius II, born Enea Silvio Piccolomini, a native of the small village of Corsignano which would later be renamed "Pienza", meaning "cittá di Pio" ("city of Pio"), in his honor.

facts.fact: It was part of the project to rebuild Pienza as an ideal city.
facts.quote: The palace, also known as the Pontifical, was commissioned by Enea Piccolomini, or Pope Pius II, to Italian Renaissance sculpture Bernardo Rossellino, as part of the project for the reconstruction of Pienza as the ideal city.

facts.fact: Rossellino took inspiration from the Palazzo Rucellai in Florence, the work of his master Leon Battista Alberti.
facts.quote: For its construction Rossellino was inspired by the Palazzo Rucellai in Florence, the work of his master Leon Battista Alberti.

facts.fact: It has a square plan on three floors, built of rough light stone.
facts.quote: It has a square plan, developed on three floors, made of rustic light stone.

facts.fact: The main entrance leads to a rectangular central courtyard with a loggia on stone columns.
facts.quote: On the ground floor there is a main entrance to the building that overlooks the central courtyard. The courtyard is rectangular with a loggia to supported by stone columns.

facts.fact: Each of the large, evenly spaced upper windows is split in two by a thin column.
facts.quote: Each window is divided into two parts by a thin column.

facts.fact: On a clear day the palace looks out over the Val d'Orcia and the hills of Monte Amiata.
facts.quote: On a clear day, you can see distant landscape of the Val d'Orcia and the hills of Monte Amiata.

facts.fact: The Arsenal, the former military complex that holds the museum, is a rectangle of brick buildings in south-east Vienna.
facts.quote: Several brick buildings in a rectangle layout make up the complex which is located on a bank south of the Landstraßer Gürtel.

facts.fact: The complex is Vienna's most distinguished group of Romantic historicist buildings, in an Italian-medieval and Byzantine-Islamic style.
facts.quote: It is the most distinguished building group of Romantic historicism in Vienna and was constructed in Italian-medieval and Byzantine-Islamic style.

facts.fact: Its construction was split into sectors, each overseen by an architect, among them Theophil von Hansen and Ludwig Förster.
facts.quote: The area was split into sectors where construction was supervised by the architects Carl Roesner, Anton Pius Riegel, August Sicard von Sicardsburg, Eduard van der Nüll, Theophil von Hansen and Ludwig Förster.

facts.fact: The Heeresgeschichtliches Museum (Museum of Military History) took until 1891 to finish.
facts.quote: The Heeresgeschichtliches Museum took until 1891 to finish.

facts.fact: The museum is an early work of Hansen, still in a more romantic style before he turned to Neo-Renaissance.
facts.quote: In his early works, such as the museum in the Vienna Arsenal, Hansen was still rather aligned to a more romantic style. In later years, he became the most outstanding representative of Renaissance-inspired historicism (Neo-Renaissance), which also came to be known as Viennese-style.

facts.fact: The Arsenal was heavily bombed in 1945 and mostly rebuilt in its original form after the war.
facts.quote: In 1945 the Arsenal was heavily damaged by bombing, however after the war most it was rebuilt into its original form.

facts.fact: The Triennale di Milano, a museum of art and design in Parco Sempione, is housed in the Palazzo dell'Arte, built 1931–1933 to designs by Giovanni Muzio.
facts.quote: The Triennale di Milano is a museum of art and design in the Parco Sempione in Milan, in Lombardy in northern Italy. It is housed in the Palazzo dell'Arte, built between 1931 and 1933 to designs by Giovanni Muzio and financed by Antonio Bernocchi and his brothers Andrea and Michele.

facts.fact: The building contains a theatre, the Teatro dell'Arte, also designed by Muzio.
facts.quote: The building houses a theatre, the Teatro dell'Arte, which was also designed by Muzio.

facts.fact: The exhibition moved from Monza to Milan in 1933 and became triennial, with Muzio's new Palazzo dell'Arte as its venue.
facts.quote: In 1933 the exhibition was relocated to Milan and the format was changed to a triennial basis. The designated venue was the new Palazzo dell’Arte designed by architect Giovanni Muzio, featuring Gio Ponti's Torre Branca.

facts.fact: The international Milan Triennial was held there thirteen times between 1936 and 1996, and again in 2016.
facts.quote: An international exhibition of art and design, the Milan Triennial, was held at the museum thirteen times between 1936 and 1996, and again in 2016.

facts.fact: A permanent museum of Italian design opened in the building in 2007.
facts.quote: A permanent museum of Italian design, the Triennale Design Museum, was opened in 2007.

facts.fact: Opus Hong Kong is a 12-storey, 42.62 m residential building completed in 2012 at 53 Stubbs Road on Hong Kong's Mid-Levels.
facts.quote: Opus Hong Kong (Chinese: 傲璇; Jyutping: ngou6 syun4) is a 12-storey, 42.62 m (139.8 ft) residential high-rise completed in 2012 at 53 Stubbs Road on Mid-Levels in Hong Kong.

facts.fact: Frank Gehry designed it with Ronald Lu and Partners for Swire Properties; it was his first residential project in Asia.
facts.quote: The project was designed by Frank Gehry in collaboration with Ronald Lu and Partners, and developed by Swire Properties. It was Gehry's first Asian residential project.

facts.fact: It holds 12 flats of 560 to 640 m², including two duplexes with pools.
facts.quote: The building consists of 12 residential units which range from 560 to 640 m2 (6,000 to 6,900 sq ft), including two duplexes with pools.

facts.fact: The site also has underground parking, rainwater recycling for irrigation and electric car charging.
facts.quote: Additional features on the 3,020 m2 (32,500 sq ft) site include underground parking, swimming pools, gyms, rainwater recycling for irrigation, and electric car charging systems.

facts.fact: A full-floor flat sold in 2012 for HK$470 million, then the most expensive apartment in Hong Kong.
facts.quote: A 580 m2 (6,200 sq ft) apartment, taking up the entire eighth floor, became the most expensive apartment in Hong Kong when it was sold for HK$470 million in August 2012.

facts.fact: The Tagblatt-Turm is a 61 m, 16-storey high-rise in Stuttgart.
facts.quote: Tagblatt-Turm (English: Daily Newspaper Tower) is a 61 m (200 ft), the 16-storey high-rise building in Stuttgart, Baden-Württemberg, Germany.

facts.fact: Designed by Ernst Otto Oßwald, it is one of Germany's earliest high-rises, built 1924–1928 of crushed stone and cement.
facts.quote: The landmark Tagblatt-Turm was designed by architect Ernst Otto Oßwald, and is one of Germany's earliest high-rises, constructed between 1924 and 1928 and made from crushed stone and cement.

facts.fact: It was planned as Stuttgart's first high-rise and the first reinforced concrete high-rise in Germany.
facts.quote: The architect Ernst Otto Oßwald planned the tower in 1924 opposite the Schocken department store as the first high-rise building in Stuttgart and the first reinforced concrete high-rise in Germany.

facts.fact: On completion it was the tallest office building in Germany.
facts.quote: Upon completion it was the tallest building in the city after the old 1905 city hall, and the highest office building in Germany.

facts.fact: Its modern design caused controversy during construction, but it is now recognised as a cultural and architectural landmark.
facts.quote: Its modern design caused controversy during construction, however, the building has since been recognized as a cultural and architectural landmark.

facts.fact: It takes its name from the newspaper Stuttgarter Neues Tagblatt, its first occupant from 1928 to 1943.
facts.quote: From 1928 to 1943, the tower was the seat of the editorship and publishing house of the Stuttgarter Neues Tagblatt, a local newspaper; the building derives its name from this original tenant.

facts.fact: After extensive renovation it became a cultural centre with several theatres in 2004.
facts.quote: In 2004, after extensive renovations, the tower was converted into a cultural center with several theatres under the name Kultur unterm Turm.

facts.fact: The UTEC campus stands at the entrance to Lima's Barranco district and is the work of Yvonne Farrell and Shelley McNamara of Grafton Architects.
facts.quote: The campus of the University of Engineering and Technology is located at the entrance of Barranco District, between the Bajada de Armendáriz, Reducto Avenue and the Paseo de la República. The building is the work of Irish architects Yvonne Farrell and Shelley McNamara of Grafton Architects, winners of the 2020 Pritzker Prize.

facts.fact: Grafton won the design competition in 2011, and the campus was built in 2015.
facts.quote: The campus, built in 2015 by Graña y Montero, was designed in 2011 by the winning architects of the UTEC International Architecture Competition, the Irish Yvonne Farrell and Shelley McNamara of Grafton Architects.

facts.fact: Supporters have called it the "modern Machu Picchu", though its design has been controversial.
facts.quote: Although it has been dubbed the "modern Machu Picchu" by supporters, the building's design has been met with controversy.

facts.fact: The brutalist building had a construction budget of US$100 million; critics attacked its "unfinished appearance".
facts.quote: The brutalist building had a budget of US$ 100 million for its construction. Its design and location have been met with controversy and criticism, as its "unfinished appearance" has been criticised and compared to the works built during Juan Velasco Alvarado's so-called revolutionary government.

facts.fact: It was built on the remains of the huaca La Viñita, the last pre-Columbian archaeological site in Barranco.
facts.quote: The construction of the UTEC was carried out on the remains of the huaca "La Viñita", the last pre-Columbian archaeological vestige of Barranco, which was located at the intersection of the Quebrada de Armendáriz and the Vía Expresa, covering some 5000 m².

facts.fact: The project won the Silver Lion at the 13th Venice Architecture Biennale.
facts.quote: The project won the Silver Lion award at the 13th edition of the Venice Biennale of Architecture.

facts.fact: The UTEC building was among the works cited when Farrell and McNamara received the 2020 Pritzker Prize.
facts.quote: In 2020, Farrell and McNamara received the Pritzker Prize; one of their selected works was the UTEC building.

facts.fact: La Congiunta in Ticino, Switzerland, is a museum built by Peter Märkli and Stefan Bellwalder that opened in 1992 to house a permanent installation of Hans Josephsohn's sculptures.
facts.quote: Permanent installations of Hans Josephsohn's works can be seen at the museum La Congiunta in Tessin, Switzerland, which was built by Peter Märkli and Stefan Bellwalder and opened in 1992.

facts.fact: The Supreme Federal Court Palace is the seat of Brazil's highest appeal and constitutional court, designed by Oscar Niemeyer with structural engineer Joaquim Cardozo.
facts.quote: The Supreme Federal Court Palace is the seat of the Supreme Federal Court, Brazilian highest appealing court and constitutional court. It was designed by architect Oscar Niemeyer and the structural project was carried out by engineer Joaquim Cardozo.

facts.fact: It stands on the Three Powers Plaza with the Palácio do Planalto and the National Congress.
facts.quote: It is part of the Praça dos Três Poderes (Three Powers Plaza), whose other buildings are the Palácio do Planalto presidential palace and the National Congress.

facts.fact: Niemeyer's Brasília buildings, all designed by 1960, were experimental and linked by shared design elements.
facts.quote: His designs for the National Congress of Brazil, the Cathedral of Brasília, the Palácio da Alvorada, the Palácio do Planalto, and the Supreme Federal Court, all designed by 1960, were experimental and linked by common design elements.

facts.fact: The building rests on side pillars and is lifted slightly off the ground, which makes the whole look light.
facts.quote: The building is supported by side pillars and is slightly elevated from the ground, giving lightness to the whole.

facts.fact: Cardozo's calculations let the foundations be thin, barely touching the ground.
facts.quote: The structural calculations by Joaquim Cardozo allowed the foundations of the Supreme Court building and other palaces, as well as of the Cathedral of Brasília, to be thin, barely touching the ground.

facts.fact: Alfredo Ceschiatti's statue "A Justiça" (1961) stands in front of the building.
facts.quote: The work "A Justiça" (The Justice) is located in front of the Supreme Court. The statue was sculpted in 1961 by Alfredo Ceschiatti.

facts.fact: It was declared a national heritage site by IPHAN in 2007, the year Niemeyer turned 100.
facts.quote: The building was declared a national heritage site by the National Institute of Historic and Artistic Heritage (IPHAN) in 2007, the year that Niemeyer turned 100.

facts.fact: The Palmach Museum in Ramat Aviv is dedicated to the Palmach, the strike force of the pre-state Haganah.
facts.quote: The Palmach Museum (Hebrew: מוזיאון הפלמ"ח) is a museum located in Ramat Aviv, Israel dedicated to the Palmach, the strike-force of the pre-state underground Haganah defense organization, which was later integrated into the Israel Defense Forces.

facts.fact: It opened in 2000 and was designed by Israeli architects Zvi Hecker and Rafi Segal.
facts.quote: Opened in 2000, the Palmach Museum commemorates the contribution of the Palmach to the creation of the State of Israel. It was designed by Israeli architects Zvi Hecker and Rafi Segal.

facts.fact: The museum is an underground series of multimedia chambers, beginning with a memorial for the fallen.
facts.quote: The museum is an underground series of multi-media experience chambers, starting with a memorial for the fallen.

facts.fact: It has an angular zig-zag plan laid out to preserve the trees on the site.
facts.quote: The Palmach Museum has an angular zig-zag plan positioned around the preservation of trees on the site.

facts.fact: It is clad in a local sandstone found while digging for the project, and was shown at the Venice Biennale.
facts.quote: It is clad in a local sandstone that was found in excavations for the project. It was exhibited at the Venice Biennale.

facts.fact: Museo Jumex, in Mexico City's Polanco neighbourhood, opened in November 2013 in a building by David Chipperfield to house the Colección Jumex.
facts.quote: The collection is housed at Museo Jumex, the main outpost of Fundación Jumex Arte Contemporáneo, located in the Polanco neighborhood in Mexico City. The museum opened in November 2013 in a building designed by David Chipperfield.

facts.fact: Zoning limits left little room, so Chipperfield put the offices, shop and library in neighbouring buildings and gave the museum almost wholly to exhibition space.
facts.quote: Zoning restrictions limited the space available, so Chipperfield put the museum administration, shop, and library in existing adjoining buildings, and devoted the Museum almost entirely to exhibit space.

facts.fact: The upper galleries take natural light from roof skylights.
facts.quote: The galleries on the upper levels receive natural light from the skylights on the roof facing toward the west.

facts.fact: The building stands on fourteen columns and is built of concrete faced with travertine from Xalapa, Veracruz.
facts.quote: The building is supported on fourteen columns, and is built of concrete covered with plaques of travertine limestone from Xalapa, in the state of Veracruz.

facts.fact: The floor-to-ceiling windows on the lower floors have stainless steel frames.
facts.quote: The floor-to-ceiling windows on the lower floors have frames of stainless steel.

facts.fact: It is part of the Plaza Carso development, across the street from the Museo Soumaya.
facts.quote: It is part of the mixed-use development Plaza Carso, which also includes a shopping mall, and sits across the street from another museum, Museo Soumaya.

facts.fact: It was designed in response to its surroundings, using materials sourced in Mexico.
facts.quote: It was conceived in response to its surroundings and local context, incorporating domestically sourced materials.

facts.fact: Palacio Barolo is a landmark office building on Avenida de Mayo in Buenos Aires, and the city's tallest building for more than a decade.
facts.quote: Palacio Barolo is a landmark office building, located at 1370 Avenida de Mayo, in the neighborhood of Monserrat, Buenos Aires, Argentina. It stood as Buenos Aires' tallest building for more than a decade until the construction of the Kavanagh Building in 1936.

facts.fact: The Italian architect Mario Palanti designed it for Luis Barolo, an Italian immigrant who made his fortune in knitted fabrics.
facts.quote: Italian architect Mario Palanti was commissioned to design the building by entrepreneur Luis Barolo, an Italian immigrant who had arrived in Argentina in 1890 and had made a fortune in knitted fabrics.

facts.fact: It follows the cosmology of Dante's Divine Comedy, out of the architect's admiration for the poet.
facts.quote: The Palacio Barolo was designed in accordance with the cosmology of Dante's Divine Comedy, motivated by the architect's admiration for Alighieri.

facts.fact: Its 22 floors are split into hell (basement and ground floor), purgatory (floors 1–14) and heaven (15–22), and it is 100 metres tall, a metre per canto.
facts.quote: There are 22 floors, divided into three "sections". The basement and ground floor represent hell, floors 1-14 are purgatory, and 15-22 represent heaven. The building is 100 meters (330 feet) tall, one metre for each canto of the Divine Comedy.

facts.fact: When completed in 1923 it was the tallest building in South America.
facts.quote: When completed in 1923, it was the tallest building, not only in the city, but also in the whole of South America.

facts.fact: The lobby's central dome opens into nine vaulted archways, standing for the nine circles of hell.
facts.quote: It radiates out from a central dome into nine vaulted archways; these represent the nine circles of hell as described in the Inferno.

facts.fact: Its rooftop lighthouse and that of its twin, Palacio Salvo in Montevideo, were meant to welcome ships entering the Río de la Plata.
facts.quote: The lighthouse on the top of the building along with the Palacio Salvo in Montevideo, Uruguay, were designed to serve as a welcome to visitors arriving from the Atlantic Ocean to the Rio de la Plata estuary, similar to the Pillars of Hercules.

facts.fact: It was declared a national historic monument in 1997.
facts.quote: This building was declared a national historic monument in 1997.

facts.fact: The Rockefeller Archeological Museum, next to Herod's Gate in Jerusalem, holds finds from excavations in Mandatory Palestine, mainly from the 1920s and 1930s.
facts.quote: The Rockefeller Archeological Museum, formerly the Palestine Archaeological Museum ("PAM"; 1938–1967), is an archaeology museum located in Jerusalem, next to Herod's Gate, that houses a large collection of artifacts unearthed in the excavations conducted in the British-ruled Mandatory Palestine, mainly in the 1920s and 1930s.

facts.fact: John D. Rockefeller Jr. agreed to give two million dollars toward the project.
facts.quote: Encouraged by Lord Plumer, the British High Commissioner, Breasted approached American philanthropist John D. Rockefeller Jr., who agreed to donate two million dollars toward the project.

facts.fact: Austen Harrison, chief architect of the Mandate's Public Works Department, designed a white limestone building blending eastern and western elements.
facts.quote: The museum was designed by Austen Harrison, chief architect of the Mandatory Department of Public Works, who drew up blueprints for a white limestone building integrating eastern and western architectural elements.

facts.fact: The foundation stone was laid in June 1930 and the museum opened in January 1938.
facts.quote: The foundation stone was laid in June 1930, and the museum opened in January 1938.

facts.fact: Eric Gill carved the reliefs over the entrance and a gargoyle fountain in the inner courtyard, as well as the stone signs in English, Hebrew and Arabic.
facts.quote: The museum features a stone bas-relief of the meeting of Asia and Africa above the main entrance together with ten stone reliefs illustrating different cultures and a gargoyle fountain in the inner courtyard carved in 1934 by the British sculptor Eric Gill (1882–1940). Gill also produced stone carved signage throughout the museum in English, Hebrew, and Arabic; the Hebrew lettering was inspired by fonts from recently discovered Second Temple-era artifacts, most prominently the Uzziah tablet, but also ossuaries from the period.

facts.fact: Its exterior mixes 1930s modern trends with traditional Middle Eastern themes; Harrison called architecture the "sculpting of space".
facts.quote: While the exterior is a wonderful amalgam of modern trends from the 1930s and traditional Middle Eastern themes, the interior is no less inspiring. Harrison once said that architecture is the "sculpting of space" and the museum is a testament to that sentiment.

facts.fact: In the 1967 war its hexagonal tower served as a lookout.
facts.quote: Seven months later, when the 1967 Six-Day War broke out, the museum was captured by an Israeli paratroop brigade. Its hexagonal tower was used as a lookout.

facts.fact: The Dead Sea Scrolls were kept there from their discovery in 1947 until 1967.
facts.quote: The Museum's most prized collection, the Dead Sea Scrolls, were housed in the Museum from their discovery, in 1947, until 1967, when, following the Israeli capture of East Jerusalem, Israel relocated the scrolls to the Israel Museum, in West Jerusalem, with the ownership of these scrolls having been heavily contested ever since.

facts.fact: Moshe Safdie designed the Yad Vashem Children's and Deportees Memorials in Jerusalem in 1995.
facts.quote: 1995: Yad Vashem Children's and Deportees Memorials, Jerusalem

facts.fact: Safdie, architect of the Holocaust History Museum, also designed the Deportees (cattle-car) Memorial.
facts.quote: Safdie is also the architect behind the Children's Memorial and the Deportees (cattle-car) Memorial.

facts.fact: The Memorial to the Deportees, known as the "train monument", remembers the Jews taken to the extermination camps in cattle cars.
facts.quote: The Memorial to the Deportees, aka "train monument", in memory of the Jews taken to the extermination camps by cattle cars

facts.fact: The 60-foot-high Kennedy memorial is shaped like the stump of a felled tree, symbolising a life cut short.
facts.quote: The 60-foot-high (18 m) memorial is shaped like the stump of a felled tree, symbolizing a life cut short.

facts.fact: Inside are a bronze relief of Kennedy and an eternal flame at the centre.
facts.quote: Inside is a bronze relief of Kennedy, with an eternal flame burning in the center.

facts.fact: It is ringed by 51 concrete columns, one for each US state and one for Washington, D.C., each with that place's emblem and separated by slim glass panels.
facts.quote: It is encircled by 51 concrete columns, one for each of the 50 states in the United States plus one for Washington, D.C., the United States capital. The emblems of the states (and of the District of Columbia) are displayed on each of the columns, and the columns are separated by slim panels of glass.

facts.fact: It was built in 1966 with money given by American Jewish communities.
facts.quote: The monument was built in 1966 with funds donated by American Jewish communities.

facts.fact: It sits on the highest of the Jerusalem hills, at 825 metres.
facts.quote: The site is located 7 miles (11 km) from downtown Jerusalem, in the same general direction as Hadassah Medical Center, on top of the highest of the Jerusalem hills, at an elevation of 825 metres (2,707 ft).

facts.fact: It was designed by architect David Resnick, later winner of the 1995 Israel Prize, with sculptor Dov Feigin.
facts.quote: Yad Kennedy was designed by the Brazilian-born Israeli architect David Resnick, who later won the 1995 Israel Prize in architecture, and the Ukrainian-born Israeli sculptor Dov Feigin.

facts.fact: Because money was raised in every US state and in Washington, D.C., the idea of a column for each led Resnick to the tree trunk, a life felled in its prime.
facts.quote: However, because money was being raised for the memorial by groups in all 50 states in the U.S., as well as groups in Washington, D.C., a vision of columns for each of those locations ultimately helped him come up with the concept of a tree trunk, linked to the idea that Kennedy's life had been cut down like a tree that is felled in its prime.

facts.fact: The Regional Theatre of Biobío in Concepción, Chile (2018) is one of Smiljan Radić's completed projects.
facts.quote: Other completed projects include the Regional Theater of Bío-Bío in Concepción, Chile (2018) and NAVE, a performing arts center in Santiago.

facts.fact: One of Fernando Távora's most important works of the 1980s was the renovation and extension of the Pousada de Guimarães, a former convent turned into the Santa Marinha historic hotel.
facts.quote: One of his most important works in the 1980s was the renovation and extension of the Pousada de Guimarães, a former convent which at the time was transformed into the Sta. Marinha Historic Hotel.

facts.fact: L'Arbre Blanc in Montpellier is listed among Sou Fujimoto's works.
facts.quote: L'Arbre Blanc, Montpellier, France, 2017 (est.)

facts.fact: The House of Music Hungary, part of the Liget Budapest project in City Park, was designed by Sou Fujimoto and opened in January 2022.
facts.quote: The House of Music Hungary, part of Liget Budapest, designed by Japanese architect Sou Fujimoto, opened in January 2022, and the Museum of Ethnography opened on 23 May 2022.

facts.fact: It stands in Budapest's City Park, a public park near the city centre.
facts.quote: The City Park (Hungarian: Városliget, pronounced [ˈvaːroʃliɡɛt]; German: Stadtwäldchen) is a public park close to the centre of Budapest, Hungary. It contains many attractions, including buildings from the 19th century, such as Széchenyi thermal bath, the Budapest Zoo and Botanical Garden, and the Capital Circus of Budapest as well as museums and other cultural institutes, including the Museum of Ethnography and the Hungarian House of Music.

facts.fact: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Stadium is a cricket stadium in Ahmedabad's Navrangpura district that hosted the first One Day International played in India.
facts.quote: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Stadium or SVP Stadium for short, sometimes referred as Sports Club of Gujarat Stadium; is an Indian sports stadium located in the Navrangpura district of Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India. The stadium hosted the first One Day International match played in India.

facts.fact: The mayor, Sheth Chinubhai Chimanbhai, hired Charles Correa to design the stadium and clubhouse, with Mahendra Raj as consulting structural engineer.
facts.quote: Sheth Chinubhai Chimanbhai, a leading industrialist and then Mayor of Ahmedabad, hired architect Charles Correa to design both the stadium and the clubhouse. The early idea for the construction of the stadium was conceived and structural engineer Mahendra Raj served as the consulting engineer.

facts.fact: Building began in 1959; money troubles meant only the roofed south pavilion was finished by 1966, and the other stands followed by the 1980s.
facts.quote: The construction of the SVP stadium began in 1959. Due to financial issues, the stadium was partially completed in 1966 with only a roof-covered south pavilion. Later the stands around the entire stadium were built by the 1980s.

facts.fact: It used a complex folded-plate structural system, the first building of its kind in India.
facts.quote: It used a complex folded plate structural system, the first such building in India.

facts.fact: The reinforced concrete folded-plate cantilever roof over the pavilion, 20 m wide and 326 feet long, was the longest such span in the world in 1963.
facts.quote: The folded plate cantilever roof above the pavilion was 20 m wide and 326 feet long. It was made of reinforced cement concrete and was the longest such span in the world in 1963.

facts.fact: Geometric concrete frames on the outside leave open space under the seats.
facts.quote: The exterior has geometric concrete frames which creates open space below the seats for the spectators.

facts.fact: In 2020 the Getty Foundation named it one of 13 significant twentieth-century buildings worldwide and gave it a grant.
facts.quote: In July 2020,  the Getty Foundation announced that SVP Stadium was one of 13 significant twentieth-century buildings in the world and announced a grant.

facts.fact: The Pakistan Monument is a national monument and heritage museum on the Shakarparian Hills in Islamabad, built to symbolise the unity of the Pakistani people.
facts.quote: The Pakistan Monument (Urdu: یادگارِ پاکستان, romanized: Yādgār-e-Pākistān) is a national monument and heritage museum located on the western portion of the Shakarparian Hills in Islamabad, Pakistan. The monument was constructed to symbolize the unity of the Pakistani people; and is dedicated to those who sacrificed their "today" for a better "tomorrow".

facts.fact: Arif Masoud's design was chosen from 21 competition entries in 2003; the monument was finished in 2006 and inaugurated on 23 March 2007.
facts.quote: From a total of 21 submissions, 3 were short-listed. The final design proposed by Arif Masoud was selected and approved on 10 July 2003. The foundation stone was laid on 25 May 2004, completed in 2006 and inaugurated on 23 March 2007 by President General Pervez Musharraf.

facts.fact: The design is rooted in Mughal architecture: its petal shapes come from the muqarnas.
facts.quote: Covering a total area of 2.8 hectares (6.9 acres), the design of the monument is rooted in the rich Mughal architecture of the Subcontinent. Its petal-shaped structure is derived from the traditional muqarnas of Mughal architecture.

facts.fact: The four large petals stand for Pakistan's four main cultures and the three small ones for minorities, Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan.
facts.quote: The four large petals represent each of the four cultures, the Punjabi, the Baloch, the Sindhi and the Pakhtun. The three smaller petals represent: the minorities, Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan.

facts.fact: The granite petals project as suspended cantilevers, and their inner walls carry artwork of Pakistan's landmarks and independence leaders.
facts.quote: The petals are built of granite (projecting in a suspended cantilever form, among the largest in Asia) and its inner walls are covered with artwork depicting various landmarks of Pakistan, notable people of Pakistan's independence movement and musical and dance themes.

facts.fact: The architect honoured the construction workers by setting their hand prints along the walls of the Freedom Plaza.
facts.quote: Though the name of the architect – Arif Masoud – is inscribed in stone on the main dedication plaque located outside the main plaza, he has honoured all construction workers by placing their hand impressions all along the long walls flanking this Freedom Plaza on both  sides.

facts.fact: From the air the monument reads as a star and crescent, like Pakistan's flag.
facts.quote: From the air, the monument looks like a star (centre) and a crescent moon (formed by walls forming the petals), these represent the star and crescent on Pakistan's flag.

facts.fact: Independence Memorial Hall is a national monument in Colombo's Independence Square, built to mark Sri Lanka's independence from British rule in 1948.
facts.quote: Independence Memorial Hall (also known as Independence Commemoration Hall) is a national monument in Sri Lanka built for the commemoration of the independence of Sri Lanka from British rule, with the restoration of full governing responsibility to a Ceylonese-elected legislature on 4 February 1948. It is located in Independence Square (formerly Torrington Square) in the Cinnamon Gardens, Colombo.

facts.fact: It stands where the first parliament was formally opened on 4 February 1948.
facts.quote: The monument was built at the location where the formal ceremony marking the start of self-rule, with the opening of the first parliament by Prince Henry, Duke of Gloucester occurred at a special podium on 4 February 1948.

facts.fact: It was designed by a group of eight architects led by Tom Neville Wynne-Jones.
facts.quote: The building was designed by a group of eight notable architects led by Tom Neville Wynne-Jones CBE, and included F. H. Billimoria, Shirley de Alwis, Oliver Weerasinghe, Homi Billimoria, Justin Samarasekera, and M. B. Morina.

facts.fact: The design is based on the Magul Maduwa, the royal audience hall of the Kingdom of Kandy, where the 1815 Kandyan Convention was signed.
facts.quote: The design of the building is based on the Magul Maduwa (Celebration Hall), the Royal audience hall of the Kingdom of Kandy the last native kingdom of the island, where on 5 March 1815 the Kandyan Convention was signed between the British and the Kandyian Chieftains (Radalas) ending the Kingdom of Kandy.

facts.fact: It served as the ceremonial assembly hall for Ceylon's Senate and House of Representatives, and now hosts the annual national day celebrations.
facts.quote: Apart from being a monument, it served  as the ceremonial assembly hall for the Senate of Ceylon and the House of Representatives of Ceylon until the parliament was moved to the new parliament complex. Currently it is the venue for religious events and annual national day celebrations.

facts.fact: A statue of D. S. Senanayake, the first prime minister, stands at its head.
facts.quote: Located at the head of the monument is the statue of the first prime minister of the country Rt. Hon. Don Stephen Senanayake "The Father of the Nation".

facts.fact: The School of the Arts is a specialised independent school in Singapore with a six-year integrated arts and academic curriculum.
facts.quote: School of the Arts (SOTA) is a specialised independent school in Singapore, offering a six-year integrated arts and academic curriculum leading to an International Baccalaureate diploma or career-related programme.

facts.fact: The campus stands at 1 Zubir Said Drive in Bras Basah, at the foot of Mount Sophia.
facts.quote: The 13-acre (5.3 ha) campus is located at 1 Zubir Said Drive in Bras Basah, along the foot of Mount Sophia.

facts.fact: The S$145 million campus was completed in 2009 and the school moved in on 4 January 2010.
facts.quote: Costing S$145 million, construction of the permanent campus was completed in 2009, and SOTA moved in on 4 January 2010.

facts.fact: WOHA completed the campus in 2009.
facts.quote: In 2009, the firm completed the School of the Arts campus in Singapore and The Met residential tower in Bangkok.

facts.fact: It was named World Learning Building of the Year at the 2010 World Architecture Festival.
facts.quote: 2010 World Architecture Festival, World Learning Building of the Year for School of the Arts

facts.fact: It won a RIBA International Award in 2011.
facts.quote: 2011 RIBA International Award for School of the Arts

facts.fact: People's Park Complex is a high-rise shopping and residential building in Singapore's Chinatown, next to Chinatown MRT station.
facts.quote: People's Park Complex (Chinese: 珍珠坊; pinyin: Zhēnzhū fāng) is a high-rise commercial and residential building in Singapore, situated in Park Road off Eu Tong Sen Street in Outram, within People's Park and next to Chinatown MRT station.

facts.fact: The newly founded Design Partnership (William Lim, Tay Kheng Soon and Koh Seow Chuan) won the commission in its first year, 1967.
facts.quote: In 1967, following the break-up of Malayan Architects Co-Partnership, William Lim set up Design Partnership (now known as DP Architects) with Tay Kheng Soon and Koh Seow Chuan. In its first year, the firm was successful with its architectural proposal for People's Park Complex.

facts.fact: The 31-storey, 103-metre building was the first shopping centre of its kind in Southeast Asia; the mall was finished in 1970 and the flats in 1973.
facts.quote: With a height of 103 metres (338 feet), the 31-storey People's Park Complex building was the first shopping centre of its kind in Southeast Asia and set the pattern for later retail developments in Singapore. The shopping centre was completed in October 1970, while the residential block was completed in 1973.

facts.fact: Its block of flats came closest in Singapore to Le Corbusier's Unité d'Habitation in Marseille, in concept and form.
facts.quote: Its name as well as the block of flats was the closest to Le Corbusier's ideal of high-rise living, as expressed in his Marseille Unité d'Habitation, both in concept and in form.

facts.fact: Its 25 residential levels were nicknamed "streets in the air", meant as places for neighbours to meet.
facts.quote: Its 25 levels have been nicknamed "streets in the air", a development of the Corbusian ideal, and are intended to offer convenient spots for social interaction and intermingling.

facts.fact: The mall holds Singapore's first "city room" or atrium, an idea pioneered by the Japanese Metabolists.
facts.quote: The shopping centre incorporates the first "city room" or atrium in Singapore, a concept that was pioneered by several Japanese architects under the Metabolist Movement in the 1960s.

facts.fact: The city room is two interlocking multi-storey atriums ringed by shops and kiosks, keeping Chinatown's busy character.
facts.quote: The shops in the shopping mall surround the large internal "city room", which consists of two multi-storey interlocking atriums, where a large number of "turn-over shops" and kiosks are located. The "city room" serves to retain the busy character of Chinatown.

facts.fact: It was originally finished in exposed raw concrete in the Brutalist style.
facts.quote: The original exterior finish of the People's Park Complex was exposed raw concrete, in keeping with the Brutalist architectural style.

facts.fact: The Singapore Conference Hall is a five-storey modernist building capped with a cantilevered V-shaped roof.
facts.quote: Designed in modernist style, the SCH is five stories tall and capped with a cantilevered V-shaped roof.

facts.fact: The Malayan Architects Co-Partnership design won a government competition in 1962; completed in October 1965, the building was the headquarters of the National Trades Union Congress.
facts.quote: The building design by the Malayan Architects Co-Partnership was selected through a competition held by the government in 1962. Completed in October 1965, the SCH hosted various conferences and exhibitions in addition to being the headquarters of the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC).

facts.fact: It was designed by Chan Voon Fee, William Lim and Lim Chong Keat, with natural ventilation built in for Singapore's tropical climate.
facts.quote: The building was designed in modernist style by three architects from the Malayan Architects Co-Partnership – Chan Voon Fee, William Lim, and Lim Chong Keat. The SCH is five stories tall and air-conditioned, with a natural ventilation system integrated into the building design due to Singapore's tropical climate.

facts.fact: The cantilevered roof and terraces rest on concrete columns, and the V-shaped roof collects rainwater into a central downpipe.
facts.quote: The building is capped with a cantilevered roof and terraces, which are supported by concrete columns. The V-shaped roof collects rainwater which drains through the central downpipe.

facts.fact: Inside, walls and ceilings use local timbers such as merbau and mersawa, and mosaic tiles in Malay mat patterns.
facts.quote: The interior walls and ceilings are crafted from local timber such as merbau and mersawa, serving as an expression of local identity. The walls are also covered with mosaic tiles of Malay mat patterns, some retained from previous renovations.

facts.fact: It is now home to the Singapore Chinese Orchestra and was the first post-colonial building gazetted as a national monument in Singapore.
facts.quote: The SCH houses the Singapore Chinese Orchestra (SCO); the concert hall has a capacity of 831 people. It was the first post-colonial building to be gazetted as a national monument in Singapore.

facts.fact: Friedrich Silaban's 1955 entry in the National Monument design competition was ranked highest by the jury but was not accepted; it took second place, with first place left vacant.
facts.quote: Silaban also took part in the National Monument design competition. While his first submission in 1955 was the highest ranked by the jury, it was not accepted and won second place while the first place went vacant.

facts.fact: In 1961 Sukarno offered Silaban and Soedarsono the project together; Silaban refused, and Soedarsono was commissioned to design the monument.
facts.quote: After a second attempt failed, Sukarno offered Silaban and another architect, Soedarsono, the opportunity to lead the project in 1961, but Silaban refused, preferring to work on the project alone. Soedarsono was eventually commissioned to design the monument.

facts.fact: The mausoleum is a large building in the centre of Ba Đình Square in Hanoi, where Ho Chi Minh read the Declaration of Independence in 1945.
facts.quote: It is a large building located in the center of Ba Đình Square, where Ho, Chairman of the Workers' Party of Vietnam from 1951 until his death in 1969, read the Declaration of Independence on September 2, 1945, establishing the Democratic Republic of Vietnam.

facts.fact: Work began on 2 September 1973 and it was inaugurated on 29 August 1975.
facts.quote: Construction work began on September 2, 1973, and the mausoleum was formally inaugurated on August 29, 1975.

facts.fact: It was inspired by Lenin's Mausoleum in Moscow but adds Vietnamese elements such as the sloping roof.
facts.quote: It was inspired by Lenin's Mausoleum in Moscow but incorporates distinct Vietnamese architectural elements, such as the sloping roof.

facts.fact: The outside is grey granite; the inside is grey, black and red polished stone.
facts.quote: The exterior is made of grey granite, while the interior is grey, black and red polished stone.

facts.fact: It is 21.6 m high and 41.2 m wide, flanked by two stepped platforms for viewing parades.
facts.quote: The structure is 21.6 metres (70 ft 10 in) high and 41.2 m (135 ft 2 in) wide. Flanking the mausoleum are two platforms with seven steps for parade viewing.

facts.fact: The embalmed body lies in a cooled central hall, in a glass case under dim light, guarded by soldiers.
facts.quote: The embalmed body of President Ho Chi Minh is preserved in the cooler, central hall of the mausoleum, which is protected by a military honour guard. The body lies in a glass case with dim lights.

facts.fact: The gardens hold nearly 250 species of plants from all regions of Vietnam.
facts.quote: The gardens surrounding the mausoleum have nearly 250 different species of plants and flowers, all from different regions of Vietnam.

facts.fact: It appears in a list of brutalist structures, credited to Garol Isakovich.
facts.quote: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, Hanoi, Garol Isakovich, (1975)

facts.fact: The Hanoi Museum was designed by gmp Architekten and built in 2010.
facts.quote: The Hanoi Museum, located in Vietnam, was designed by GMP Architekten and built in 2010.

facts.fact: The museum has the shape of an inverted pyramid.
facts.quote: The Hanoi Museum and Hong Kong Coliseum are buildings which have an inverted pyramidal shape.

facts.fact: It shows the history of Hanoi over 1,000 years and the culture and heritage of Vietnam.
facts.quote: As a museum, it represents the artifact of Hanoi over 1000 years, and it also displays the culture and heritage of Vietnam.

facts.fact: The Singapore Sports Hub (2014) is among the most notable stadium projects led by Arup.
facts.quote: The most notable stadium projects led by Arup remain the City of Manchester Stadium (2002), Allianz Arena (2005), Beijing National Stadium (2008), Donbas Arena (2009) and the Singapore Sports Hub (2014).

facts.fact: Arup's design and engineering work on the Singapore Sports Hub won a 2013 World Architecture Festival award in the Future Projects, Leisure category.
facts.quote: Arup's multidisciplinary sports venue design and engineering scope on the Singapore Sports Hub won the 2013 World Architecture Festival Award in the Future Projects, Leisure Category.

facts.fact: The National Arts Theatre in Iganmu, Lagos, is a full copy of the Palace of Culture and Sports in Varna, Bulgaria, by the same architect, Stefan Kolchev.
facts.quote: A complete copy of the "Palace of Culture and Sports" exists in Africa - this is the "National Arts Theatre", Iganmu, in Lagos, Nigeria. The building was designed by the same architect - Stefan Kolchev.

facts.fact: Its Bulgarian original in Varna was completed in 1968.
facts.quote: The Palace of Culture and Sports was completed in 1968.

facts.fact: The Voortrekker Monument is a granite structure on a hilltop just south of Pretoria, commemorating the Voortrekkers who left the Cape Colony between 1835 and 1854; Gerard Moerdijk designed it.
facts.quote: The granite structure is located on a hilltop, and was raised to commemorate the Voortrekkers who left the Cape Colony between 1835 and 1854. It was designed by the architect Gerard Moerdijk.

facts.fact: It was inaugurated on 16 December 1949 by Prime Minister D. F. Malan.
facts.quote: The monument was inaugurated on 16 December 1949 by Prime Minister D. F. Malan.

facts.fact: It is 62 metres high on a 40-by-40-metre base, recalling the Dôme des Invalides and the Völkerschlachtdenkmal but with African influences.
